finding.title: Replace DateTime.now() with a fixed date in curriculum_progress_service_test.dart track seeding
finding.why: TQ-6 bans wall-clock reads in tests. These two fields are never asserted on, so the file is not currently flaky, but the pattern is copy-pasted into the non-batch sibling test/features/progress/data/repositories/progress_repository_test.dart (15 further DateTime.now() occurrences), normalizing non-determinism that will bite the day someone adds a time-based assertion against this seed.
finding.recommendation: Replace both DateTime.now() calls with a fixed literal, e.g. DateTime.utc(2026, 1, 1), matching every other file in this batch.
acceptance_criteria: grep 'DateTime.now()' on the file returns no matches.

finding.title: Rewrite track_dual_progress_reactivity_test.dart so it stops overriding the provider it claims to guard
finding.why: Both tests replace trackDualProgressMetricsProvider's own body with a stub that independently calls ref.watch<int>(completionCommittedProvider) itself (lines 27, 69). A Riverpod .overrideWith fully replaces the provider's create function, so the real body in lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart:357 is never invoked by either test. Deleting that real ref.watch<int>(completionCommittedProvider) line today — silently breaking the dashboard/progress-hub's live refresh after a completion — would not fail either test in this file, despite the file's own docstring calling itself 'Regression test for Fix 3'. Contrast with the correctly-built sibling recent_activity_reactivity_test.dart, which drives the real production provider body over a real in-memory DB with no override of the provider under test.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite using the recent_activity_reactivity_test.dart pattern: real in-memory DB, unmodified trackDualProgressMetricsProvider, seed a completion, tick completionCommittedProvider, assert the provider's actual output changes.
acceptance_criteria: Test constructs trackDualProgressMetricsProvider without overriding that same provider family
Test goes red when ref.watch<int>(completionCommittedProvider) is deleted from lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart:357

finding.title: Log the two silent catch blocks in lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart via AppLogger
finding.why: Both catches swallow every exception with no AppLogger call. If programCalendarPositionProvider throws (line 430-431), overdueCount/todayDueCount silently become 0 — a falsely reassuring 'nothing overdue' on the dashboard per-track row — with zero breadcrumb to diagnose it. If getScopedContent throws inside _safeLoadLeavesForTrack (line 648), the track just vanishes from trackDualProgressMetricsProvider's output with no trace. The same file already fixes this exact anti-pattern under the F20 label for _safeLoadLeaves/_safeHeLabelLookup (lines ~570-609, which log via AppLogger.warning with event/fields/exception/stackTrace) — these two catches were never brought in line with that established, documented convention.
finding.recommendation: Log both catches via AppLogger.warning(event:, exception:, stackTrace:) before falling back, matching the F20 pattern used elsewhere in the same file.
acceptance_criteria: Both catch blocks call AppLogger before returning/defaulting
No 'catch (_) {' block in lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart lacks an adjacent AppLogger call

finding.title: Remove or wire up the dead MonthlyActivitySliverCalendar spike before its placeholder class collides with the real Drift companion
finding.rule: dead code / AG-4 (future duplicate top-level name)
finding.why: grep across lib/ and test/ shows MonthlyActivitySliverCalendar is imported nowhere except its own file and its own 171-line test (monthly_activity_sliver_calendar_test.dart) — 404 + 171 = 575 lines maintained since commit 2b2eeb54 (2026-05-20) for zero product value; the widget's own doc comment admits 'not wired into any screen yet'. Worse, its hand-rolled `class MonthlyActivityRollup` is explicitly a stand-in 'until build_runner generates the companion' — but the real monthly_activity_rollups Drift table (already committed, not yet added to UserDatabase's table list) declares @DataClassName('MonthlyActivityRollup'), the identical name. The day someone finishes wiring that table into UserDatabase and runs build_runner, this hand-written class and the generated one collide.
finding.recommendation: Either finish wiring MonthlyActivityRollups into UserDatabase now and switch the widget onto the generated class, or delete the spike widget, its table, and its test until the feature is scheduled.
acceptance_criteria: MonthlyActivitySliverCalendar is either reachable from a real screen route or removed along with its test and orphaned table
No hand-written class reuses a name reserved by a table's @DataClassName annotation

finding.title: Batch trackDualProgressMetricsProvider's per-track sequential DB reads (N+1 left un-fixed by sibling F13)
finding.why: Each loop iteration awaits _safeLoadLeavesForTrack (itself up to 4 sequential DAO calls: getScopesByTrack, getScopes x1-2, getActiveTracksForProfile, lines 618-648), then completionPercent (397), getCompletionsByTrackAndProfile (406), getEntriesByTrack (408), getProgramForProfileAndCurriculum (421), and conditionally programCalendarPositionProvider (430-431) — up to 9 sequential DB round-trips per track, none parallelized via Future.wait. A profile with 5 active tracks does ~40-45 sequential awaits to render the Progress-hub/Dashboard per-track section, and this provider re-runs on every completionCommittedProvider tick (line 357, i.e. after every single completion mark). The very same file already fixed this exact N+1 shape for the sibling lifetimeDataProvider under the F13 label (completionsByProfileForLifetimeProvider / priorImportsByProfileProvider, lines 78-138) but the batching was never extended here. Actual latency impact is unmeasured (SUSPECTED) — the un-batched pattern itself is CONFIRMED by static reading.
finding.recommendation: Batch the per-track queries the way F13 batched lifetimeDataProvider's — one profile-wide query per DAO partitioned in memory by trackId — or parallelize the independent per-track work with Future.wait.
acceptance_criteria: trackDualProgressMetricsProvider issues O(1) queries per DAO (or explicitly parallelizes per-track work), not O(tracks) sequential awaits
A ProviderObserver-based test mirroring lifetime_knowledge_screen_test.dart's F13 test asserts each batched provider builds once across N tracks
